translationRepairs: At the time grand mentor and recorder of the masters of writing affairs, Prince of Zhao commandery Rui, had long lived inside the palace and shared counsel at the curtain. Zicong knew He Shikai resented Rui and general-in-chief of the guards Prince of Huai'nan Lou Dingyuan and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on provincial duty and strip Dingyuan of the guard command. He answered, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign too received the throne from his predecessor. Every minister's wealth came from the sovereign father and son. Leave the great men inside the court unchanged, and the princes and dukes below will surely have no other wish.

At the time grand mentor and recorder of the masters of writing affairs, Prince of Zhao commandery Rui, had long lived inside the palace and shared counsel at the curtain. Zicong knew He Shikai resented Rui and general-in-chief of the guards Prince of Linhuai Lou Dingyuan and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on provincial duty and strip Dingyuan of the guard command. He answered, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign too received the throne from his predecessor. Every minister's wealth came from the sovereign father and son. Leave the great men inside the court unchanged, and the princes and dukes below will surely have no other wish.
s0039 titles Lou Dingyuan 臨淮王; 臨淮 is Linhuai, not 淮南 (Huai'nan). The proposed swap restores the correct princely title without other changes.

At the time Grand Mentor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs Prince of Zhao commandery Rui had long dwelt within the palace and took part in counsel at the curtain; Zicong had long known He Shikai resented Rui and General-in-Chief of the Guards Prince of Huai'nan Lou Dingyuan, and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on external appointment and strip Dingyuan of guard authority; therefore he answered, saying, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign likewise received the throne from the former emperor. Every minister's wealth and rank came from father and son's grace to the sovereign. If the honored men within the court are left wholly unchanged, the princes and dukes below will surely harbor no other intent.

At the time Grand Mentor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs Prince of Zhao commandery Rui had long dwelt within the palace and took part in counsel at the curtain; Zicong had long known He Shikai resented Rui and General-in-Chief of the Guards Prince of Linhuai Lou Dingyuan, and feared they might forge the final edict to send Rui out on external appointment and strip Dingyuan of guard authority; therefore he answered, saying, "The late emperor was Gao Huan's son, and the present sovereign likewise received the throne from the former emperor. Every minister's wealth and rank came from father and son's grace to the sovereign. If the honored men within the court are left wholly unchanged, the princes and dukes below will surely harbor no other intent.
The same 臨淮王 in the literal field was rendered Huai'nan; Prince of Linhuai matches the Chinese place-name and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing with an edict of rebuke; Tang Yong was held in custody, then soon released.
Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulü Xiaoqing with an edict of rebuke; Tang Yong was held in custody, then soon released.
s0110 names 斛律孝卿; 斛律 is Hulü and 孝卿 is Xiaoqing. “Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing” wrongly doubles 孝 and omits the ü; Hulü Xiaoqing is the accurate form.
Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing to proclaim an edict rebuking and reproaching him; Yong was detained in custody and soon released.
Anaigong slandered him and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulü Xiaoqing to proclaim an edict rebuking and reproaching him; Yong was detained in custody and soon released.
Literal likewise mistook 斛律孝卿 as Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing; Hulü Xiaoqing corrects the surname and given name without altering the rest.
As the emperor was about to visit Jinyang, an edict put Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing in overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters himself and did not consult or report upward.
As the emperor was about to visit Jinyang, an edict put Hulü Xiaoqing in overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters himself and did not consult or report upward.
s0111’s 孝卿 is the same Hulü Xiaoqing introduced in s0110; “Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing” repeats the doubled-孝 error, and Hulü Xiaoqing restores the correct name.

As the imperial carriage was about to visit Jinyang, an edict ordered Xiaoxiaoqing to take overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters on his own and did not consult or report upward.
As the imperial carriage was about to visit Jinyang, an edict ordered Xiaoqing to take overall charge of cavalry expenditures; he decided most matters on his own and did not consult or report upward.
The literal short form 孝卿 is Xiaoqing, not Xiaoxiaoqing; replacing the doubled reading fixes the given-name error while keeping the sentence otherwise unchanged.
Tang Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and resented Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing's slight; he stayed at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.
Tang Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and resented Hulü Xiaoqing's slight; he stayed at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.
s0114 again writes 斛律孝卿; changing Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing to Hulü Xiaoqing corrects the name and matches the Chinese.

Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and hated that Hulu Xiaoxiaoqing slighted him; he therefore remained at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.

Yong feared Anaigong would slander him again and hated that Hulü Xiaoqing slighted him; he therefore remained at Jinyang and, with Moduolou Jingxian and others, elevated the Prince of Ande as emperor.
Literal 斛律孝卿 requires Hulü Xiaoqing; the proposed replacement removes the false Xiaoxiaoqing reading without other alterations.
Within a day or two the city fell; Tang Yong surrendered to Zhou and, by precedent, was made Pillar of State and grand general.
Within a day or two the city fell; Tang Yong surrendered to Zhou and, by precedent, was made Yitong Grand General.
s0115 awards a single office 儀同大將軍 (Yitong Grand General). “Pillar of State and grand general” invents 柱國 and splits one title into two; Yitong Grand General is accurate.
